# Yang--Mills Representational Dynamics Research Package

Version: 2026-07-21

This archive collects the complete output of a representation-aware research
programme on the Yang--Mills existence and mass-gap problem. It contains the
philosophical ontology, mathematical representation calculus, Clay-target
decomposition, successive restricted-model attacks, executable calibrations,
tests, and theorem-status ledgers.

The package contains seventy-seven compiled PDFs (405 pages), their LaTeX sources,
fifty-nine stage-level machine-readable theorem dependency graphs plus six
cross-stage frontier graphs, forty-nine numerical calibration datasets,
stage-level computational modules with 978 recorded passing tests, 51 additional
publication-supplement checks.  It also contains five independent publication
plans with 193 completed self-contained todos and a clean-install-tested export
of all 30 Yang--Mills workflow skills for the Codex IDE extension in VS Code
and Codex CLI.  Stage 52 adds twelve passing dependency-free hypothesis and
substrate regression tests, Stage 53 adds fifteen passing H1 regression tests,
and Stages 54--58 add fifty-two passing downstream tests.  Stages 68--77 add
194 independently rerun and audited hypothesis-stream tests.  The complete
package contains 1,390 files, of which 1,389 are
recorded in the checksum ledger (the ledger excludes itself).

## Epistemic status

This package is a research programme and a restricted theorem suite. It does
not construct four-dimensional continuum Yang--Mills theory and does not prove
the Clay mass-gap problem.

The proved contributions include finite spectral lemmas, representation-error
composition, a heat-kernel translation obstruction, an exact two-plaquette
`U(1)` bridge, the Gaussian retained/fiber response split, an exact multiscale
covariance decomposition, an independent-defect cluster bound, and finite
product total-variation comparison. Continuum clustering and spectral transfer
results are explicitly conditional on hypotheses recorded in the ledgers.
The quotient/fiber restricted theorem gives an explicit four-dimensional cubical
`SU(2)`-compatible quotient/fiber block: exact cochain and retained-map ranks,
a positive fiber curvature spectrum, exact centered Gaussian cancellation, and
a local nonlinear heat-kernel stability theorem under a quantified small-chart
budget.  It is a local finite-block result, not a continuum construction.
The one-step refinement then proves an exact effective-action recursion from a
five-component derivative norm: it controls fiber coercivity, centered
transport, the Hessian generated by marginalization, and a declared defect
channel while transporting states and observables exactly.
The heat-kernel initialization stage then removes the existential constant
from the exact radial one-plaquette `SU(2)` action, supplies explicit Hessian
and third-derivative budgets, and encloses a gauge-invariant bad-curvature
probability with analytic series tails.
The nonlinear block-geometry stage transports that radial result through the
actual four-factor quaternion plaquette map.  It proves an explicit local
Coulomb slice, a bi-Lipschitz curvature chart on the `2^4` physical quotient,
sharp finite incidence aggregation, and a complete five-component good-chart
input accepted by the one-step recursion.  Its probability calibration also
shows that this first certified chart is far too small for a full-measure
claim, localizing the next obstruction at the chart/polymer overlap.
The ultraviolet-overlap stage then shows that this mismatch is not structural.
At heat time `3e-6`, a Haar-augmented nonlinear action certificate and a
standalone heat-kernel/independent-block weighted-polymer benchmark are
simultaneously strict.  This removes a scale-incompatibility objection while
isolating the first unproved implication more sharply: a volume-uniform
dependent activity theorem for the complete four-dimensional link measure.
The frustrated-conditioning stage then falsifies the most direct proposed
bridge to that theorem.  An exact center-valued conditioning on the `2^4`
block produces five identity staples and one `-I` staple around a selected
link.  The resulting conditional law has density `p_t(U)^5 p_t(-U) dU` and
concentrates at class angle `pi/6`, leaving the frustrated plaquette at angle
`5pi/6`.  Thus a bad-plaquette probability cannot be uniformly small over all
microscopic conditionings.  A viable replacement must retain and charge the
frustrating boundary through good collars, multi-link integration, or typed
center/topological contours.
The good-collar stage proves that a common bi-invariant geodesic
`eta`-ball for `m` staples restores the conditional rate gap
`rho^2-m eta^2`; the Stage 10 center-frustrated boundary has coherence radius
exactly `pi/2` and is therefore excluded from the ultraviolet collar.
The center-charging stage then reconstructs the erased boundary cost on the
exact `GF(2)` cubical complex.  The Stage 10 pattern requires exactly five
negative plaquettes, while every nonempty exact center cocycle has at least
three.  Its Bianchi contour graph uses common-three-cell adjacency of degree
20, deliberately distinguished from the shared-link bad-event graph.
The dependent-Gaussian stage retains the complete linearized gauge dependence:
curvature has covariance `t P tensor I_3`, with `P` the projection onto
`im(d_1)`.  A joint exponential-moment argument gives a rooted connected-event
bound without independence and is strictly subcritical at the frozen
ultraviolet witness.
The nonlinear-transfer stage proves an abstract two-channel event
envelope with
`q_eff=exp(kappa-J)+exp(-K)`.  The sufficient targets `kappa<=0.2` and
`K>=7` close its one-scale counting gate, but those full nonlinear `SU(2)`
inequalities were left open.
The nonasymptotic good-collar stage then restores all finite-time prefactors.
It proves an explicit one-link `SU(2)` bound, but shows that the declared
degree-18 weight is reached only near `t=8.9942e-7`, not at the frozen
`t=3e-6` witness.
The continuous-charging stage proves that collar failure forces an incident
curvature above `eta/2` and total incident energy above `eta^2/2` for every
selected-link value.  Combining this with good-collar admissibility yields a
frozen exponent only `0.9339`, quantitatively ruling out the simplest local
one-link repair for the required collar rate.
The chart-comparison stage proves normalized Gaussian-to-nonlinear event
comparison.  The local action oscillation is tiny, but the currently certified
408-dimensional inner-ball coverage loses `3.7188` per plaquette, exposing a
gauge-atlas and normalization problem rather than a local Hessian problem.
Finally, the adaptive-domination stage proves that history-uniform conditional
bad-block bounds imply Bernoulli stochastic domination and the desired cluster
sum.  A two-site counterexample proves intersection moments alone are
insufficient.  The revised first open implication is therefore a concrete
adaptive multi-link `SU(2)` conditional bound, not an unspecified activity
construction.
The state-weighted transfer stage then shows that scalar worst-history
conditioning is stronger than connected-defect control requires.  A positive
boundary-state weight transports rare entry cost through forced later
transitions, with exact connected-set summability and a two-state example whose
scalar ceiling is one but weighted ceiling is subcritical.
The boundary-disintegration stage supplies its exact finite interface:
relative tree gauge removes interior redundancy while retaining a
boundary-covariant connection, exact Haar factorization, and an interior
conditional fiber.
The local-typical-set stage replaces the Stage 17 global `408`-ball by
dependency-safe local Gaussian constraints.  The required four-link radius is
`0.00602316`, and a two-center radius-`pi/2` atlas covers all of `SU(2)` with
explicit Haar-Jacobian ratio.
The sharp-overlap stage computes the exact plaquette-log identity Hessian norm
`1+sqrt(2)` in the package's quaternion Lie-algebra convention and transports
it using the certified third derivative.  It
proves fiber contraction and generated-base coercivity at the required local
typical radius, closing the finite local overlap gate.  Normalized conditional
density comparison and state-weighted multi-link complement charging remain
open.
The local-cylinder comparison stage then replaces the obsolete global
`408`-ball normalization by the dependency-safe event already supplied by the
typical-set atlas.  Its frozen centered-reference loss is only
`3.01676e-5` per support unit, so the remaining issue is uniformity over
retained nonlinear boundary states rather than local Gaussian coverage.
The multichannel state-weight stage solves the exact entry/persistence
Lyapunov problem for center, continuous, cut/orbit, and topology channels.  It
shows that a target weighted ceiling `q` with forced return requires total
entry budget of order `q^2`, and that persistence must itself be below `q`.
The one-scale `K+R` stage proves the positive-kernel composition law and finds
a strict feasible budget at radius `0.00614956`, inside the sharp nonlinear
window.  Finally, the partition-ratio stage reduces the physical obstruction
to one boundary-uniform free-energy inequality with required charge
`F_*>6.71292101139`.  Entropy-cancellation and retained-normalizer
counterexamples prove why deterministic action charge alone cannot establish
it.
The Haar-entropy stage then computes the exact local denominator cost
`v(r)=(r-sin(r)cos(r))/pi` and proves nonasymptotic cubic entropy brackets.
The coherent-optimizer stage replaces an uncertified denominator search by the
unique stationarity equation `v'(delta)/v(delta)=m(eta+delta)/t`; after
re-optimizing the `K+R` radius, the coherent continuous channel fits strictly
inside the one-scale budget, conditional on collar coherence.  The
coherence--charge stage proves an overlap-correct multi-witness exponent and
then finds a quantitative incompatibility: the coherent estimate permits only
`eta<=0.00717145`, while a degree-18, overlap-one incoherent contour needs
`eta>=0.00893686` for the required free energy.  The channelwise frontier
therefore identifies the next exact target as a canonical sector-aware witness
polymer on a charge--entropy remedy curve: at unit charge its effective degree
must be at most `2.20542`, while retaining degree 18 requires charge
amplification at least `1.55295`.  No physical channel is yet closed uniformly
in retained state and volume.
The dispersion-witness run then corrects the collar-failure charge by the exact
Fréchet identity: covering failure costs more than `eta^2`, twice the Stage 16
energy bound. Restoring radial entropy falsifies the resulting action-only
plaquette promotion, but the exact dependent-Gaussian staple-dispersion
spectrum produces a genuine common RMS interval
`[0.00386371990242, 0.00717145149149]`. This calculation keeps the complete
projected curvature dependence and does not assume independent plaquettes.
The run also supplies a canonical incidence-four plaquette witness, an exact
weighted repair-congestion theorem, adaptive retained-state filtration, a
five-channel numerator atlas, and six independent periodic `GF(2)` center-flux
carriers. Its first unproved implication is one explicit nonlinear,
history-uniform multichannel comparison/repair inequality. Integer bundle
topology, one-scale basin entry, repeated RG, continuum construction, and the
mass gap remain open.
The nonlinear-transfer run now converts the restricted Gaussian dispersion
window into an exact curved-chart statement.  Within a common geodesic ball,
pairwise staple dispersion and Karcher variance differ only by the certified
factor `(sin r/r)^2`; normalized density comparison then transports the
nonlinear high-dispersion event into the centered retained reference.  The
resulting restricted continuous-channel probability is
`7.757562504510382e-5`, strictly below its allocated ceiling
`0.0009721110007367992`.
An independent repair route was tested rather than assumed.  Centered tangent
contraction has enough ideal action gain, but its minimum-norm lift to links
has a worst external-curvature spill coefficient `1.635983263598`, exceeding
the admissible `0.9683231479404556`; hence the generic single-star repair is
falsified on the certified block.  The package also proves exact periodic
center-flux barriers and exhibits an integral Pfaffian charge invisible to all
center labels.  These results sharpen, but do not close, the physical target:
the first open implication is a boundary- and history-uniform normalized
density comparison together with a chart-complement bound for the full
positive-mass retained-state table.  Center-sector ratios, cut/orbit control,
nonabelian integer topology, basin entry, repeated RG, continuum construction,
and the mass gap remain open.

The conceptual-restrategy stage then audits the full programme, formalizes a
minimal region--scale operator-system substrate, and runs executable first
probes of ten aggressive hypotheses.  Coordinated central-four and all-eight
interior-link constraints acquire numerical zero-spill directions even though
the orientation-correct one-star problem has none; this revives collective
polymer cancellation as a testable backup without proving a boundary law.
An exact integral-flux collision further shows that center labels plus a total
Pfaffian charge are not compositionally sufficient under blocking.  The
highest-reward primary target is now a vacuum-weighted, normalized,
multichannel retained-state kernel inequality.  The stage remains C1/C2 and
does not establish physical basin entry, RG iteration, a continuum theory, or
a mass gap.

The H1 vacuum-weight stage then develops the highest-reward hypothesis through
its complete finite and conditional chain.  It corrects the original
orientation: a positive vacuum eigenfunction normalizes temporal transfer,
while its inverse is the natural forward cost of entering vacuum-suppressed
states.  For a masked bad kernel this choice cancels vacuum-amplitude ratios
exactly.  Separately, Collatz--Wielandt proves that the Perron vector of a fixed
bad subkernel is the optimal positive Lyapunov weight, without identifying it
as a physical vacuum.  The existing four-channel star certificate is exactly
Perron-optimal with weighted ceiling `0.002430277501841998`, scalar ceiling
one, and strict degree-18 branching ratio `0.8702225337961371`.  The first
remaining implication is construction and uniform control of the complete
normalized nonlinear `SU(2)` retained-state kernel and its root moment; the
stage does not prove basin entry, continuum construction, or a mass gap.

The five-target H1 downstream run then closes the finite normalized-kernel
interface, a sufficient Harnack/root-moment theorem, robust multichannel
Perron envelopes, and the changing-state-space weight cocycle.  It quantifies
the four-channel uncertainty budget and supplies two decisive obstructions.
First, fixed contraction per geometrically growing RG level is power-law in
terminal physical scale unless contraction is calibrated to accumulated
physical length.  Second, a fixed one-scale spatial defect ceiling is
compatible with positive temporal transfers whose gaps tend to zero; positive
regulated gaps may also collapse after conversion to physical units.  The run
therefore reaches C2 with C3 conditional bridges.  The first open physical
implication remains construction of the complete boundary-uniform normalized
nonlinear `SU(2)` kernel and a cutoff-uniform root-weight moment.

The hypothesis-stream portfolio then separates H2--H10 into nine independent
research tracks, each with its own report, theorem graph, and implementation
backlog.  The separation exposes several new strategic constraints: H2
requires invariance of physical decay under tempered representation changes;
H3's multi-star zero-spill modes remain C1 until an orientation-correct
boundary law exists; H4 proves that full six-component integer flux data are
contextually necessary; H6 supplies a typed square-defect telescoping theorem;
and H9/H10 isolate observable density and recovery from finite correlation
tests.  These streams are plans and restricted theorems, not additional
physical Yang--Mills claims.

The follow-on parallel execution in Stages 68--77 advances every H1--H10
stream to its next falsification gate.  After an independent frontier audit
and required-fix pass, all 194 tests pass.  The strongest global level remains
C2: exact or tolerance-qualified restricted-model theorems.  The combined run
rules out three especially tempting shortcuts: a small same-measure masked
defect ceiling need not imply a temporal gap; finite observable recovery need
not give OS-norm density; and a positive RG-step exponent need not remain
positive in physical units.  Stages 78--79 record the audit, dependency graph,
test registry, and the next reward-ranked physical targets.

## Directory map

### `01_conceptual_foundations`

Four matched `.tex`/`.pdf` documents covering conceptual difficulty,
phenomenon-preserving representations, relational ontology, and the
representation-aware Clay programme.

### `02_relational_rigidity_program`

The main representation calculus, original detailed research plan, proof
ledger, theorem dependency graph, finite spectral implementation, and tests.

### `03_heat_kernel_basin_entry`

The first frontier attack: heat-kernel influence theorem, compact-group and
regulator calibrations, two-tier basin proposal, dependency graph, and tests.

### `04_fibered_block_rg`

The interacting-block refinement: retained/fiber distinction, two-plaquette
bridge implementation, covariance decomposition, defect and regulator bounds,
frontier ledger, and tests.

### `05_su2_quotient_fiber`

The explicit four-dimensional (2^4) cubical block: linearized cochain and
retained-curvature matrices, exact rational rank checks, quotient/fiber
spectral calibration, a local `SU(2)` heat-kernel theorem, frontier ledger,
dependency graph, implementation plan, and tests.

### `06_one_step_effective_action`

The exact finite-dimensional one-step theorem: a typed retained/fiber action
norm, Brascamp--Lieb effective-Hessian transfer, centered-fiber response,
state/observable transport, gauge-covariance and defect certificates, Gaussian
Schur-complement calibration, frontier audit, and hostile tests.

### `07_su2_heat_kernel_initializer`

The exact one-plaquette initializer: matched `SU(2)` character and Poisson-image
representations, analytic image truncation, explicit local Hessian and third
derivatives, a chain-rule block interface, gauge-invariant curvature tails,
frontier audit, calibration, and hostile tests.

### `08_su2_nonlinear_block_geometry`

The nonlinear `2^4` bridge: unit-quaternion product/logarithm calculus, exact
incidence and Hodge constants, a quantitative local Coulomb slice, a
bi-Lipschitz plaquette-curvature chart, refined heat-kernel action aggregation,
all five Stage 06 local norm components, a restricted-model and limit audit,
probability-overlap calibration, frontier ledger, and hostile tests.

### `09_su2_uv_overlap`

The ultraviolet decision stage: a cancellation-free Poisson-image tail bound,
local link-Haar Hessian and third-tensor estimates, the Haar-augmented
five-component norm, a 216-plaquette block union benchmark, a weighted
independent connected-activity theorem, a strict coexistence witness, a
declared parameter search, a topology/dependence ledger, and fail-closed tests.

### `10_frustrated_conditioning_obstruction`

The dependent-measure obstruction stage: an exact `GF(2)` center-staple
surjectivity certificate, the induced one-link conditional heat-kernel law, a
closed small-time large-deviation rate theorem, log-domain numerical
calibration, a replacement-strategy ledger, dependency graph, frontier audit,

### `51_publication_portfolio`

Four independent publication work packages: the frustrated-conditioning
obstruction, the verified nonlinear quotient--fiber block, proof-bearing
representational dynamics, and explicit `SU(2)` heat-kernel enclosures.  The
portfolio contains 153 unique todos, per-paper theorem contracts, source
corpora, literature and novelty audits, manuscript architectures, rigorous
numerics requirements, stop/go gates, definitions of done, a machine-readable
registry, and a validator.  Paper 4 has an explicit standalone-or-merge gate
so that weak material is incorporated into Paper 2 rather than submitted as an
artificially separate result.  A shared manuscript-automation layer now
separates motivation and introduction, literature grounding, proof
development, proof-appendix construction, and automated LaTeX/PDF production.
The renderer scaffolds modular sources, lints citations and references,
compiles with `latexmk`, validates PDF metadata and extracted text, renders
preview pages, and emits a JSON build report.

Paper 01 has now been implemented as a self-contained 21-page blinded
manuscript.  Its main theorem covers compact connected gauge groups with a
nonidentity central element, proves open positive-measure stability, and
derives the exact microscopic Dobrushin row obstruction.  The publication
bundle includes proof and novelty ledgers, a primary-source literature audit,
an exact incidence verifier, PDF previews, a venue memo, and a cover letter;
its conservative frontier classification is `C2`.

Paper 02 has now been implemented as a self-contained 18-page blinded
manuscript.  On a fixed side-two four-dimensional cube it uses rooted tree
gauge to obtain an exact product-Haar quotient, verifies the retained/fiber
ranks and a rational curvature lower bound by two independent exact kernels,
and proves one local-cylinder marginalization with explicit response and
effective-Hessian constants.  Its proof, literature, novelty, reproducibility,
venue, and frontier audits are packaged with the source and PDF.  The theorem
is deliberately classified `C2`: it does not control the full interacting
chart complement, iterate the renormalization step, or imply a mass gap.

Paper 03 has now been implemented as a self-contained 27-page blinded
philosophy-of-physics manuscript. It introduces typed certificate profiles for
preservation, approximation, forgetting, recovery, and uniformity; proves a
conditional recovery-to-spectrum theorem; and supplies exact hidden-sector,
collapsing-gap, and noncommuting-limit countermodels. Its Yang--Mills chain
identifies the separate obligations between lattice regulation, gauge descent,
RG, continuum Schwinger data, OS reconstruction, and spectral interpretation.
The abstract theorem is classified `C3` conditional representation transfer,
while the Yang--Mills application remains `C0` methodology and supplies no
continuum construction or unconditional mass gap.

Paper 04 has now been implemented as a self-contained 13-page technical note.
It proves explicit uniform bounds for every requested finite derivative order
of the central `SU(2)` heat-kernel action, propagates the paired-image bounds
through the logarithm by Bell polynomials, treats the cut locus in a separate
paired chart, and derives an exactly normalized Haar tail. Its order-eight
certificate uses rational arithmetic for all pass decisions and is checked by
17 hostile tests plus an independent character/image diagnostic. This is a
`C2` local analytic result, not an interacting RG or mass-gap theorem.

Paper 05 is implemented as a self-contained 15-page mathematical-physics
note.  It identifies gauge-covariant Fréchet staple dispersion with residual
geodesic-quadratic link energy, proves the nonlinear spherical comparison, and
replaces the exploratory star spectra by orientation-correct rational
certificates.  On every interior link of the open side-two four-cube, the
centered Gaussian covariance spectrum is
`0, 239/630 (x2), 33/70 (x3)` and the minimum external-curvature lift spectrum
is strictly positive, `37/33 (x3), 391/239 (x2)`.  The vanished zero-spill mode
from the earlier calculation is documented as an orientation error.  This is
a `C2` finite-block result held for external novelty review, not a nonlinear
physical-measure or continuum theorem.
